## ✨ New Features

### SharedString now allows applications to configure which snapshot format it uses ([#28370](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28370))

Use `configuredSharedString` to select a snapshot format through the registered DDS factory. Set `newMergeTreeSnapshotFormat` to `true` for flat snapshots or `false` for legacy snapshots. Both snapshot formats remain supported.

```typescript
import { configuredSharedString } from "@fluidframework/sequence/legacy";

const ConfiguredSharedString = configuredSharedString({
  newMergeTreeSnapshotFormat: true,
});
const factory = ConfiguredSharedString.getFactory();
```

Register this kind, or its factory, in place of the default SharedString. The API is also available from `fluid-framework/legacy`. Omit the factory option to allow the runtime option or loaded snapshot format to determine the format.

The existing configuration-provider flow remains supported:

```typescript
const configProvider = {
  getRawConfig(name: string): boolean | undefined {
    return name === "Fluid.Sequence.newMergeTreeSnapshotFormat"
      ? true
      : undefined;
  },
};
```

Return `false` for this flag to explicitly select legacy snapshots. Selection precedence is the configuration flag, the factory option, the runtime option, then the loaded snapshot format. When no explicit setting is provided, new SharedStrings use the legacy format and loaded SharedStrings reuse the format identified by their snapshot header. A summary written in the selected format becomes the inherited format for clients that load it without an explicit setting. Configuration and options are fixed for each DDS instance; use a new client or factory configuration to select a different format. No additional DDS attributes are stored for the setting. Format selection does not force an otherwise unchanged DDS to produce a new summary.

## 🌳 SharedTree DDS Changes

### Revert to a commit directly from branch history ([#28399](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28399))

Commit metadata now has a `revertTo()` method that reverts later changes on the branch from which the commit was obtained. This supersedes the existing `revertTo()` API on the view (though that API remains available).

```typescript
// Given some arbitrary commit in the history of a particular view...
const commit = view.branchHistory.getHead()?.getParent();
// ...check whether that commit can still be reverted, then revert if so
if (commit?.revertTo === undefined) {
  throw new Error("Sorry, the requested revert can't be completed");
}
commit.revertTo();
```

If the commit is no longer reachable on its original branch, the original branch has been replaced or disposed, or a later commit changes the schema, then the revert is not possible. In any of these cases, the `revertTo()` method will be absent (`undefined`) from the commit metadata object. The method is also unavailable while a transaction is in progress or during change events. Read `revertTo` from the commit metadata before each call rather than retaining the function; each obtained function can be called only once.

Custom metadata supplied to transactions and reverts is read and serialized while edits to the target checkout are disallowed. Getters and serialization hooks that attempt to edit that tree throw an error before the edit is applied.

### Plain and formatted text nodes support moving character ranges ([#28440](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28440))

The [PlainText.Members](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/plaintext-namespace/members-interface) API now exposes `moveRangeToIndex`, matching the existing [TreeArrayNode.moveRangeToIndex](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/treearraynode-interface#moverangetoindex-methodsignature) operation. Both plain text and [formatted text](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/formattedtext-namespace/members-interface) nodes can now reorder ranges of text without removing and reinserting characters.

```typescript
import { PlainText } from "@fluidframework/tree/alpha";

const text = PlainText.Tree.fromString("abcdef");
text.moveRangeToIndex(4, 0, 2);
console.log(text.fullString()); // "cdabef"
```

### Resolve historical node selections and text positions for presence ([#28446](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28446))

The new alpha `TreeViewAlpha.locations` API allows capturing a _location_ on one view and resolving it in another view (possibly one on a different client). The resolved position accounts for intervening edits and moves. The primary use case for this functionality is for presence scenarios. Selections can target entire nodes (e.g. "whole paragraph," or "todo item") or a gap within a sequence of nodes (e.g. "text caret position").

The following pseudocode illustrates how an application may use this API.

```typescript
// Use an attached main view with acknowledged edits and no open transaction.
const capture = view.locations.capture([
  { kind: "node", node: selectedImage },
  { kind: "sequence", node: characters, index: focusIndex },
  { kind: "sequence", node: characters, index: anchorIndex },
]);

// Send to another client, typically using the presence API.
publishSelection({ capture });

// On receipt, with the editor model synchronized to the local tree:
const results = view.locations.resolve(message.capture);
for (const entry of results) {
  if (entry.status === "resolved") {
    const location = entry.location;
    if (location.kind === "node") {
      highlightNode(location.node); // A local SimpleTree object.
    } else {
      showCaret(location.node, location.index); // Current array and gap.
    }
  }
  // Otherwise, entry.status is "unavailable" and entry.reason explains why,
  // or entry.status is "revision-unavailable".
  // The receiving client may be behind the sender: retry after applying
  // the inbound operations for that revision.
  // If the revision has expired instead and been trimmed, wait for a fresh presence update.
}

// Single locations do not require arrays.
const caret = view.locations.captureGap(characters, focusIndex);
const caretResult = view.locations.resolve(caret);
const selectedNode = view.locations.captureNode(selectedImage);
```

`capture` and `resolve` accept either one location or an array and return the corresponding single result or array. The array overloads have identical per-location semantics and are more performant for many locations captured from the same revision.

Captures are opaque JSON-serializable payloads designed for transmission between clients of the same SharedTree. Their representation is hidden with `ErasedType`; applications should transmit them unchanged (but are free to nest them within other presence data). For more details on the full API surface and current limitations, see the [TreeLocationResolver documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/blob/main/packages/dds/tree/src/simple-tree/api/locations.ts).

### Unhydrated array range moves preserve content when the destination overlaps the source ([#28441](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28441))

Calling [`TreeArrayNode.moveRangeToIndex`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treearraynode-interface#moverangetoindex-methodsignature) with a destination gap inside the source range now leaves an [`Unhydrated`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/unhydrated-typealias) array unchanged, matching the resulting array contents in the hydrated case. Previously, these moves could reorder the array incorrectly and emit change deltas that did not match its content.

The destination gap is a position between items before the move, not an index in the resulting array. For example, calling `array.moveRangeToIndex(1, 0, 2)` on an array containing `["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]` now leaves that array unchanged. These overlapping moves do not emit change events on unhydrated arrays. Hydrated arrays may still emit change events even though their content remains unchanged.

### Capture and resolve presence positions in plain and formatted text ([#28466](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28466))

The alpha `TreeLocationResolver.captureGap` method and `kind: "sequence"` capture inputs now accept `PlainText.Tree` and schemas produced by `FormattedText.createSchema`, including subclasses, as well as array nodes.

```typescript
const selection = view.locations.captureGap(view.root.text, 2, {
  affinity: "after",
});
// selection can be resolved on another client, typically after being sent using presence APIs.
const result = otherView.locations.resolve(selection);
```

Text-based gap locations treat the string as a sequence of characters and have semantics analogous to those documented for sequences. Their resolved indices are character indices within the string (see the documentation on `PlainText.Members` for the distinction between character indices and UTF-16 code-unit indices).

### Support record and map formatting in formatted text ranges ([#28458](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28458))

`FormattedText.Members.formatRange` now supports record and map format nodes in addition to object format nodes. Updates preserve entries not included in the update. Set an entry to `undefined` to remove it. Map formats accept either an object containing entries or a readonly map. Node-valued properties and entries are cloned independently for each atom, including when copied from an existing hydrated format. This also fixes copying hydrated node-valued properties in object formats.

```typescript
text.formatRange(0, 5, { bold: true });
text.formatRange(0, 5, { bold: undefined });
// For map formats:
text.formatRange(0, 5, new Map([["bold", true]]));
```

### Add optional checksums to help catch unintended schema changes ([#28462](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28462))

SharedTree adds an optional schema checksum to help catch unintended view schema changes, ideally during the testing stage.

The checksum is a hash saved in application code to guard against unintended schema changes. To enable this check, pass the saved hash as `expectedHash` to the separately imported [`identifySchema`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree#identifyschema-function) function and provide its result as the optional [`schemaIdentity`](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/tree/treeviewconfigurationalpha-class#schemaidentity-property). Calling `identifySchema()` without an expected hash enables schema hash telemetry without a construction check.

#### Configure the expected hash

To set the initial hash, use a non-empty placeholder and run a test that constructs the view. Replace the placeholder with the computed hash from the error message.

```typescript
import {
  identifySchema,
  SchemaFactoryAlpha,
  StagedSchemaUpgradePolicy,
  TreeViewConfigurationAlpha,
} from "fluid-framework/alpha";

const sf = new SchemaFactoryAlpha("com.example");
const stagedNumber = sf.staged(sf.number);
class Note extends sf.object("Note", {
  text: sf.types([sf.string, stagedNumber]),
}) {}
const stagedUpgradePolicy = StagedSchemaUpgradePolicy.enabledStagedUpgrades(
  stagedNumber.metadata.stagedSchemaUpgrade!,
);

const expectedSchemaHash = "replace-with-computed-hash-from-error";

const config = new TreeViewConfigurationAlpha({
  schema: Note,
  stagedUpgradePolicy,
  schemaIdentity: identifySchema({
    // Optional.
    expectedHash: expectedSchemaHash, // Optional: enables the hash check.
  }),
});
// Throws if expectedHash does not match the current schema hash.
const view = tree.viewWith(config);
// initialize and upgradeSchema emit the target hash in Fluid Framework telemetry when schemaIdentity is provided.
view.initialize({ text: "Hello" });
```

Keep the expected hash fixed until a schema change is intentional. If a test reports a mismatch, review the schema change. If the change is intentional, update the expected hash with the computed hash from the error message.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

### Keep unresolved version marks pending when history is inconclusive ([#28448](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28448))

Version marks are no longer permanently classified as unresolvable when a historical operation read is empty or starts after the mark's sequence-number lower bound. Neither result proves that the specific batch sequenced in the unavailable range. The runtime keeps the mark pending so a disconnected or resubmitted batch can still sequence and resolve later. Hosts own retry suppression and expiration policy for long-lived pending marks.

## Legacy API Changes

### Stop recognizing pre-symbol in-memory Fluid handles ([#28418](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28418))

In-memory handles created by Fluid Framework client `2.0.0-rc.3.0.0` or earlier are no longer recognized by `isFluidHandle` or accepted by `toFluidHandleInternal`. Applications that dynamically load Fluid layers should ensure all loaded layers use `2.0.0-rc.4.0.0` or later.

### Identify a data store's package path, for use in telemetry ([#28375](https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/issues/28375))

The legacy-beta `getDataStorePackagePath` function lets callers add the containing data store's package path to diagnostic telemetry. For example, the path can identify the package containing a component that takes a long time to load. The package path is diagnostic information, not an input that configures the runtime. If the data store's snapshot details are not yet available, the lookup may fetch an omitted snapshot and read its attributes blob. This work can add latency and affect the timing of other operations, so avoid awaiting the lookup on a latency-sensitive load path. It does not resolve the handle, load the data store, or include the package path of a DDS.

```typescript
import { getDataStorePackagePath } from "@fluidframework/runtime-utils/legacy";

const packagePath = await getDataStorePackagePath(containerRuntime, handle);
```
